text:
Evan Li: Hey — first day, trying to run docker-compose for the local stack (postgres + redis) but postgres init scripts aren't running and the container keeps exiting. Docker logs show permission denied on /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata/init.sql. Using Mac M1, Docker Desktop 4.x. Anyone know a quick fix or who I should ping? Also not sure if I should be using host networking or socket path. Thanks!

Priya Rao: Welcome Evan! Most likely a bind-mount permissions issue on mac. Quick try: sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ./pgdata && docker-compose up -d postgres — the container's postgres user needs to be able to write. Also check you set PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata in the compose file.

Maya Chen: If you can, use a named volume instead of a host bind-mount to avoid mac permission headaches. In docker-compose.yml:
```
volumes:
  pgdata:
    driver: local

services:
  postgres:
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```
That tends to be less flaky for M1.

Sam O'Neil: If the init scripts in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d aren't running, make sure they're readable and have the right extension (.sh/.sql). Quick debug: ```docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/db:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro postgres:15 ls -l /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d``` to confirm they mount and are visible.

Evan Li: I tried chown to 1000 and the container starts now, but the DB logs say "Database directory appears to contain a database; Skipping initialization" — so my init user creation didn't run. How do I nuke and recreate cleanly?

Priya Rao: Run: ```docker-compose down -v``` then ```rm -rf ./pgdata/*``` (double-check path) and then ```docker-compose up -d``` to force fresh init. If you used a named volume before, you may need `docker volume ls` + `docker volume rm <name>` or `docker volume prune`. Be careful — that removes data.

eng-infra-bot: FYI — there's a devbox guide with compose snippets and troubleshooting at https://redwood.internal/dev/dev-local-db.md. It covers Mac-specific tips and common chown/prune steps.

Maya Chen: Also check .env.local for POSTGRES_PASSWORD/POSTGRES_USER mismatch vs your init script. If the directory already contains DB files the entrypoint won't re-run init scripts. Happy to screenshare if you'd like.

Sam O'Neil: Note on socket vs host: if your app runs on host (not in a container) use host.docker.internal as the DB host on mac. If app is in the same compose network, use the service name (postgres). :thumbsup:

Evan Li: thanks everyone — that got me unblocked. I'll cleanup volumes and try the named volume flow. Pinged Maya for a quick screenshare if I hit anything else.
